transcript: Doctor: What happened? Patient: I fell off my bicycle about two hours ago. I landed on my right hand and wrist. It's really swollen and I can't move it. Doctor: Did you hit your head or lose consciousness? Patient: No, I was wearing a helmet. Just my wrist. Doctor: Any numbness or tingling in your fingers? Patient: A little bit in my thumb and index finger. Doctor: Okay, let me examine you. Right wrist is significantly swollen with obvious deformity. Tenderness over the distal radius. Radial pulse is intact, capillary refill under 2 seconds. Sensation is diminished over the radial nerve distribution but motor function is intact. X-ray shows a displaced distal radius fracture, Colles type, with dorsal angulation of approximately 25 degrees and 5 millimeters of shortening. No ulnar fracture. Assessment: Displaced Colles fracture, right distal radius, with mild radial nerve paresthesia. Plan: Conscious sedation with ketamine 1 milligram per kg IV. Closed reduction under fluoroscopy. Post-reduction splint, sugar tong. Post-reduction X-ray to confirm alignment. Ibuprofen 600 milligrams every 8 hours and acetaminophen 1 gram every 6 hours for pain. Orthopedic follow-up in 5 days. Return precautions for increasing numbness or compartment syndrome symptoms.
reference_soap:
DIALOGUE:
Doctor: What happened?
Patient: Fell off bicycle 2 hours ago, landed on right hand/wrist. Swollen, unable to move.
Doctor: Head injury or LOC?
Patient: No, was wearing helmet.
Doctor: Numbness or tingling?
Patient: Some in thumb and index finger.

SUBJECTIVE:
Patient fell off bicycle 2 hours prior, FOOSH injury to right wrist. Denies head injury or LOC (helmeted). Reports swelling, inability to move wrist, mild numbness in thumb and index finger.

OBJECTIVE:
Right wrist: Significant swelling with visible deformity. TTP over distal radius.
Vascular: Radial pulse intact, cap refill <2s
Neuro: Diminished sensation radial nerve distribution, motor intact
X-ray: Displaced distal radius fracture, Colles type. Dorsal angulation ~25°, 5mm shortening. No ulnar fracture.

ASSESSMENT:
Displaced Colles fracture, right distal radius, with mild radial nerve paresthesia

PLAN:
1. Conscious sedation (ketamine 1mg/kg IV)
2. Closed reduction under fluoroscopy
3. Sugar tong splint post-reduction
4. Post-reduction X-ray
5. Ibuprofen 600mg q8h + acetaminophen 1g q6h
6. Ortho follow-up in 5 days
7. Return precautions: increasing numbness, compartment syndrome signs
